svg.title: The walker on gcd.mote with 6 and 4: the node it is at, and the values in the symbol table

g.title: Before the walk: analysis has made an entry for i and for j, and neither has a value yet. The walker starts at the first statement.
read i#1: the walker reads 6 from the input and keeps it in entry 1 of the table, the one the node points at.
read j#2: the walker reads 4 from the input and keeps it in entry 2 of the table, the one the node points at.
while: its condition, i != j, is 6 != 4: true, so the walker runs the body.
if: i > j is 6 > 4: true, so the walker takes the first branch.
:= i#1: the walk goes down to the - node and its two names, takes 6 and 4 from their entries, and puts 2 in entry 1.
Back at the while: its condition, i != j, is 2 != 4: true, so the walker runs the body.
if: i > j is 2 > 4: false, so it takes the else branch.
:= j#2: the walk goes down to the - node and its two names, takes 4 and 2 from their entries, and puts 2 in entry 2.
Back at the while: 2 != 2 is false. The loop is done, and the walker goes on to the next statement.
write: i#1 points at entry 1, which holds 2; the walker prints it. ./mote on 6 4 prints 2 too.
